title: Report
description: The Phase 1 inspection report for one scan (task B9), written by the pipeline (B10) and the report builder (B11). Code picks the verdict from a truth table; Claude writes `summary.text` from words only (S5). Every stored finding of the scan appears exactly once: in `findings` (a model judged its state), `not_inspected` (nobody looked at it, I3) or `insufficient_evidence` (looked at, could not be judged, with the reason, I4). No probability number appears anywhere: confidence is a word (I6). A vision finding is a suspect; only a meter reading proves or rules out (I1, I2).

build_id.description: Unique per report build (report.publish); a later revision of the same build (the fix, the mesh) keeps it. A patch applies only while the row still carries its build's id (created_at has whole seconds).

verdict.description: Picked in code (repairos.report.verdict truth table), never by a model. no_problems_seen (V8): nothing judged shows an issue and the capture covered the object well (config/verdict.yaml), but some regions were not checked: they are listed in verdict_reason.caveat.

code.description: issues_found: at least one region shows a potential issue (or a meter reading confirmed one). all_inspected_ok: every region was judged and none shows an issue. no_regions: nothing was captured or detected to judge. nothing_inspected: regions exist but no model could judge any. some_not_inspected: nothing judged shows an issue, but some regions were not inspected or could not be judged (coverage poor). nothing_seen_wrong: the same, with the object covered well (V8).

rule.description: The truth-table row that decided, e.g. V3.

text.description: Why, in plain words (no numbers; it is sent to the summary writer).

caveat.description: What was not checked, with counts, e.g. 'Nothing looked wrong in the 2 areas Lea could see clearly. 3 areas need a closer photo.' Shown with the verdict as its caveat list; not sent to the summary writer.

written_by.description: Model id that wrote the text.

from_words_only.description: true when the writer received words only (S5), checked in code before the call. false when the text came from the design engine, which judged the scan against the product's own design.

findings.description: Regions a model judged: an issue, or `none` (looked at, no visible issue). Ranked in code, most likely problem first (repairos.report.build.rank_key); cosmetic issues are in `cosmetic`.

most_likely.description: The finding_ids of the top rows of `findings` with an issue (at most three), ranked in code: safety > functional, then issues Jev judges as explaining the symptom, then confidence, then how many photos show it (repairos.report.build.rank_key). The app and exports lead with these.

cosmetic.description: Issues the vision model judged cosmetic (looks worn but would not stop the device working). Listed apart; they never make the verdict potential_issues on their own.

setup.description: Setup and assembly states (category setup: a battery missing, a cable unplugged, a cover not clipped), each with its plain fix. Not a broken part: listed apart and they never make the verdict potential_issues on their own. A setup state that is a hazard (severity safety: a battery in backwards, a loose mains wire) stays in `findings`.

not_inspected.description: Regions nobody looked at (I3), each with the reason. Never shown as ok.

insufficient_evidence.description: Regions looked at that could not be judged (I4), each with the reason.

next_step.description: The one next action code chose from Jev's judgments (repairos.fusion), when there is one.

target.description: What the step is about, so the app can open the meter sheet filled in. Same fields as next-action `target`.

net.description: Net name from the product's design.

power_state.description: off for continuity and resistance; on for voltage (S4).

expected.description: What a good reading looks like, compared in code (S5).

safety.description: Safety notes chosen by code from the findings (repairos.report.safety); shown before anything else.

limits.description: What photos cannot tell (always shown), plus a meter suggestion when a reported symptom is not explained.

bottom_not_placed.title: Bottom (not placed on the model)
bottom_not_placed.description: Findings from a flipped (object-moved) segment, the mini-scan of the bottom, that the backend could not line up with the main scan: they are real findings, listed in their buckets as usual, but have no 3D point on the model. Each comes with its crop so the app can show it as a photo. Absent when every such segment was aligned or the scan has none. Why a segment was not aligned: capture.segments[].why_not.

finding_id.description: The report row (in findings, cosmetic or insufficient_evidence).

issue.description: The row's issue (findings and cosmetic rows); absent for insufficient_evidence rows.

photo.description: The still and crop box the finding was seen in.

depth_source.description: lidar when the scan or a still carries ARKit depth; none otherwise (A8: sizes cannot be claimed).

stills_inspected.description: Stills with at least one region a model judged.

coverage_words.description: The phone's coverage hint in words, or 'not measured'.

views.description: Where the camera was (keyframes and stills) on the view dome around the object box (repairos.report.coverage): cells of 3 rings x 12 sectors seen, distinct sectors, and the share of cells. Absent when no box or pose is known.

segments.description: Capture segments where the object was moved (the flipped mini-scan of the bottom) and how the backend registered each to the main scan by shape (repairos.recon.segment_align). An aligned segment's findings are placed on the same model; an unaligned one's are listed in findings_not_placed with no 3D point. Absent when the scan has no such segment.

aligned.description: True when the backend registered the segment to segment 0 and placed its photos in segment 0's frame.

fitness.description: Share of the segment's object points within 1.5 voxels of segment 0's after registration.

rmse_mm.description: RMS distance of those matched points, millimetres.

why_not.description: Why the segment was not registered (aligned false).

findings_not_placed.description: Findings from this segment's photos that have no 3D point because the segment is not aligned (empty when aligned).

models.description: Provenance: which model (and version) did each step, or why a step did not run.

object.description: What the object is, from the first photos (one vision-model call; a label photo is read). Brand and model only as printed or recognised beyond doubt, else absent.

category.description: A short generic kind of product, or unknown.

label_visible.description: A model label, rating plate or printed name was readable.

mesh.description: The scan's 3D mesh for the 3D view: LiDAR TSDF, decimated, vertex-coloured, in the frame of every finding's location (pins sit on it as they are).

url.description: Gateway path: GET it with the device token (/v1/scans/{scan_id}/mesh?rev=N).

rev.description: Goes up when the mesh is rebuilt (more photos added to the scan).

format.description: Binary little-endian PLY: float x y z, uchar red green blue per vertex; triangle lists.

cloud_url.description: The object's part of the phone's LiDAR cloud, coloured points (binary PLY: float x y z, uchar red green blue), same frame (/v1/scans/{scan_id}/cloud?rev=N).

hero.description: What to show as the 3D view: points (cloud_url), mesh (url), or photos when the object is too small or too little was captured for 3D to read as the object.

design.description: Present when the design engine judged this scan against the product's own design; required when a row names `grain` or the summary says it is not words only. `project` is the design the scan was judged against.

reference_hints.description: Optional: where to look first, from public references about the identified product (web search titles and descriptions only; no third-party image or page is kept). Never evidence: a hint never makes a finding.

fix.description: Optional "Fix it": where to buy the part of the top finding, from a public shopping search (repairos.references.parts). Only title, displayed price, seller and link are kept; no page, text or image. Added when the search is ready; never evidence and never delays the report.

part.description: The part searched for, in generic words (the top finding's part class).

price.description: The displayed price; absent when the result showed none (a web result, not a shopping one).

guide_link.description: A public replacement guide for that part, when the search found one.

user_lead.description: Optional: what the person said they suspected and what the photos showed about it (repairos.references.leads.user_lead). The guess is a lead, never evidence: it only ordered the inspection; this section cites findings and never adds or changes one.

said.description: The person's own words (typed or spoken).

suspect.description: The part or area they suspected, in their generic words.

checked.description: confirmed = a judged region of that area has an issue; not_seen = regions of that area were judged with no visible issue; could_not_check = no photo of it was judged (or no area was named).

evidence_finding_ids.description: The report rows this is based on (any section).

note.description: One or two plain sentences, written in code from the rows cited.

allOf.description: A row judged by the design engine, or a summary it wrote, names the design it was judged against.

then.description: Looks good only when at least one region was judged (in `findings`, `cosmetic` or `setup`), every region was judged, and none shows an unresolved functional or safety issue.
No problems seen only when at least one region was judged and none shows an unresolved functional or safety issue; unchecked regions may remain (listed in the caveat).

box_px.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in the still's full-resolution pixels.

location.description: Where the region is on the scan: the crop box through the still's pose onto the scan (repairos.locate). `not_computed` says why there is none; a location is never made up.

frame.description: The scan's frame: metres, Y up.

point_m.description: Where the box's centre lands on the scan.

region_min_m.description: Axis-aligned box of the region on the scan.

normal.description: Unit surface normal facing the camera (mesh ray cast only).

distance_m.description: From the still's camera to point_m.

notes.description: The locator's reasons for its confidence word.

proof.description: Only a meter reading proves or rules out (I1, I2).

judgment.description: Jev's judgment of this subject, ranked in code (Suspect), in words.

explains_symptom.description: Jev's judgment, in a word, of whether a problem with this subject would explain the reported symptom (code bands the noul: fusion.questions.band).

part_class.description: Generic class (vision/generic_classes.py), never a product name. For a row judged by the design engine: the design's own name for the part.

issue.description: none = a model looked and saw no issue. Every other value is Finding.state: a suspect.

inspected_by.description: Stages that looked at this region. A judged region always includes a state judge (vlm, classifier, meter or grain). grain: the design engine judged it against the product's own design (scan measurements, photos, readings).

crop.description: The photo and box the region was seen in. Absent for a row the design engine judged from the scan's measurements, not from a photo.

severity.description: How much the issue matters (the vision model's word per crop; absent = not judged, treated as functional). Cosmetic issues are listed in `cosmetic`, never in `findings`.

part_words.description: Plain words that let a person find the part in the photo.

category.description: Finding.category: defect (also when absent) = something looks broken, damaged or faulty; setup = a setup or assembly state, not a broken part: a battery missing or in backwards, a cable or connector unplugged or not fully in, a cover not clipped, a screw or fuse missing (repairos.vision.assembly). Code decides it from the state, never a model word.

fix.description: For a setup finding: the plain fix a person can do, in one sentence (e.g. 'Put the batteries in, then test again.'). Shown to the user.

fix_plan.description: The fix for this row as data, so the app can show a card with a button instead of a sentence: what to do, what to buy, which file to print, or which meter check settles it. `fix` stays the same fix in one sentence. Absent when the design engine offered no fix for the row.

action.description: buy: order a replacement; remake: print or machine the part again from the design's file; reseat: put it back in place; rewire: fix a wire or connection; check: measure with a meter first.

summary.description: The action in one plain line.

steps.description: Short steps, in order, for reseat and rewire.

options.description: Where to buy it (action buy), from the design's bill of materials.

part_file.description: The part's own file from the design (action remake). The phone gets it from the gateway, GET /v1/scans/{scan_id}/fixes/{finding_id}/file?format=; it never holds the design engine's address or key.

check_action_id.description: The next-step action id of the meter check that settles this row (action check).

outcome.description: What the person said after trying the fix for this row (POST /v1/scans/{scan_id}/outcome). Set by the gateway when the report is read, never by the design engine; it is also the label the design engine learns from.

finding_ids.description: A collapsed row: the findings of one physical issue (same still and overlapping crops, or the same place on the scan across stills) with the same issue, finding_id first. Each finding appears in no other row (MS1).

regions.description: How many findings this collapsed row stands for.

crops.description: The crops of the other findings in a collapsed row (`crop` is the first).

merged_by.description: Why the findings of a collapsed row are one issue.

superseded_ids.description: Findings of the same place on the scan that could not be judged in another photo (insufficient_evidence) and are judged in this row's photo instead, e.g. a closer photo added later to the same scan. They appear in no other row (MS1).

allOf.description: 0 regions shown ok (or with an issue) that no model looked at.

finding_id.description: The finding of this row; for a grouped row, the first of `finding_ids`.

regions.description: How many detector regions this row stands for. Absent means one.

finding_ids.description: A grouped row: every finding it covers, finding_id first. Each appears in no other row (MS1).

not_inspected.description: One row of regions nobody looked at (I3). A row stands for one region, or, when `finding_ids` is present, for every not-inspected region of one still grouped into one row (so real findings are not buried under many small regions); `regions` is then the exact number of detector regions it covers.

finding_ids.description: A collapsed row: findings of the same place on the scan that could not be judged in any of their photos, finding_id first. Each finding appears in no other row (MS1).
